name: p4-0409-app-play-stages
title: One app host through the application play
spec: 1600-wide SVG, four stage columns for one app host with serial one at a time and max_fail_percentage 0. pre_tasks: assert app_version is a tag or commit SHA, touch drain flag under /var/www/lb-drain delegated to the first web host, pause 5 seconds. tasks: group and user, directory skeleton, git fetch pinned version, venv from requirements.lock, env file mode 0600, alembic upgrade head run_once, systemd unit, switch current symlink, meta flush_handlers, uri readyz retries 20 delay 3, prune old releases. post_tasks: remove drain flag, host back in rotation. handlers: restart fleetapp only when something changed. Orange only on the readyz check gate before post_tasks.
anchor: ## 5. The application play: release directories and an atomic switch
alt: Four columns showing pre_tasks, tasks, post_tasks and handlers for one app host, with a readiness check before the host returns to the load balancer.
cap: The host is drained first, built and switched next, and returned to rotation only after the readiness check passes.

name: p4-0409-three-db-limits
title: Three layers that limit database access
spec: 1600-wide SVG, three stacked layers between app hosts and PostgreSQL on db01. Layer listen_addresses = localhost plus ansible_host limits the network interface. Layer pg_hba.conf host db_name db_user app host /32 scram-sha-256 limits the client address. Layer ufw allow tcp 5432 from each app host limits the port at the firewall. A client arrow from an app host passes all three; a second arrow from an unlisted host is stopped. Orange on pg_hba layer only.
alt: Three stacked layers, interface, client address and firewall port, that an app host must pass to reach PostgreSQL.
cap: Interface, client address and firewall port are three separate limits, and an unlisted host is stopped by them.

name: p4-0409-expand-contract
title: Expand and contract migration during a rolling update
spec: 1600-wide SVG timeline with three phases and two lanes, old code and new code, both reading one database. Phase 1 expand: add the new piece in a way old code ignores. Phase 2 move the code over with serial rolling, old and new run side by side. Phase 3 contract: later remove the old piece. A warning box: a migration that removes a column old code still uses breaks old code mid-rollout. Note: alembic upgrade head runs once with run_once on the first host. Orange on the warning box.
anchor: ## 5. The application play: release directories and an atomic switch
alt: A three-phase timeline of expand, move code, then contract while old and new code share one database.
cap: Migrations must stay compatible with the previous release because old and new code run together during a rolling update.

name: p4-0409-venv-vs-container
title: Venv deployment versus container deployment
spec: 1600-wide SVG two-column comparison. Left Ansible-built venv: git pinned to tag or commit SHA, venv from requirements.lock inside the release directory, systemd unit, rollback by app_version or repointing current. Right container: docker_container pinned by digest sha256, restart_policy unless-stopped, healthcheck, read_only true, cap_drop ALL, no-new-privileges, memory 1g. Footer: at a fleet of containers Kubernetes takes over, Ansible keeps the node layer. Orange on the digest pin.
alt: Two columns comparing a venv release on a host with a digest-pinned container.
cap: A digest names the exact image, while a tag can be moved to a different image later.

name: p4-0409-deploy-troubleshoot
title: Failed deploy symptom checks
spec: 1600-wide SVG rows of Symptom and Checks from the table: Service fails to start (journalctl -u fleetapp -n 100, systemctl status, run ExecStart manually as app user, env file mode); 502 or 504 from nginx (curl upstream, nginx -t, ss -ltnp, ufw status); Migrations failed mid-way (backward compatible, fix forward, run_once, backup); Different results per host (pip freeze, ansible-inventory --host); Playbook slow (fact gathering, apt updates, git clone per host, forks, pipelining); Handler restarted too often (non-idempotent templates, two handlers on one topic); Rolling update killed traffic (LB not drained, no graceful shutdown, no readiness check, serial too large). Orange on the first row only.
alt: A table of failed-deploy symptoms with the checks to run for each.
cap: Match the symptom, run its checks in order, and collect evidence before changing anything.

name: p4-0409-safety-run-ladder
title: Safety command ladder before and after a release
spec: 1600-wide SVG vertical ladder of seven commands from the chapter: --syntax-check, ansible-lint playbooks/, --check --diff preview, real run, second run expect changed=0 except intentional tasks, canary app.yml -e app_version=v1.4.3 --limit app01, rollback app.yml -e app_version=v1.4.1. Side box on the second-run step listing causes of changed on rerun: command without changed_when, lineinfile regex mismatch, templates with timestamps, state latest, git on moving branch with force. Orange on the second-run step.
alt: A ladder of seven commands from syntax check to rollback with the causes of a noisy second run.
cap: A quiet second run is what lets you trust a loud first run.
